passages.text: Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to Christians in Rome.
Paul taught that Jesus Christ is Lord.
Paul said that those who are in Christ Jesus are not condemned.
Now, there is no condemnation for people who belong to Christ Jesus.
passages.original: Οὐδὲν ἄρα νῦν κατάκριμα τοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: For in Christ Jesus the law of the Spirit of life set you free from the law of sin and death.
passages.sermon:
Christ Jesus is Lord.
The Spirit gives life in Christ Jesus.
This Spirit has a law.
The law of the Spirit brings freedom.
The law of sin and death brings bondage.
The law of the Spirit set you free.
You are free from the law of sin.
You are free from the law of death.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ νόμος τοῦ Πνεύματος τῆς ζωῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ἠλευθέρωσέν σε ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ τοῦ θανάτου

passages.text: For what the law was powerless to do in that it was weakened by the flesh, God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin. He thus condemned sin in the flesh, so that the righteous standard of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.
passages.sermon:
The law could not save us.
The law was weak because of our sinful flesh.
God acted where the law could not.
God sent His own Son.
God sent His Son in the likeness of sinful flesh.
God sent His Son as an offering for sin.
God condemned sin in the flesh through His Son.
God did this so the righteous requirement of the law would be fulfilled in us.
We do not live according to the flesh.
We live according to the Spirit.
passages.original: τὸ γὰρ ἀδύνατον τοῦ νόμου ἐν ᾧ ἠσθένει διὰ τῆς σαρκός ὁ Θεὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ Υἱὸν πέμψας ἐν ὁμοιώματι σαρκὸς ἁμαρτίας καὶ περὶ ἁμαρτίας κατέκρινεν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ἐν τῇ σαρκί ἵνα τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ νόμου πληρωθῇ ἐν ἡμῖν τοῖς μὴ κατὰ σάρκα περιπατοῦσιν ἀλλὰ κατὰ πνεῦμα

passages.text: Those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh; but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.
passages.sermon:
Some people live according to the flesh.
These people set their minds on the things of the flesh.
Other people live according to the Spirit.
These people set their minds on the things of the Spirit.
passages.original: Οἱ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ὄντες τὰ τῆς σαρκὸς φρονοῦσιν οἱ δὲ κατὰ πνεῦμα τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος

passages.text: The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace, because the mind of the flesh is hostile to God: It does not submit to God’s law, nor can it do so.
passages.sermon:
The mind of the flesh leads to death.
The mind of the Spirit leads to life and peace.
The mind of the flesh is hostile to God.
The mind of the flesh does not submit to God's law.
The mind of the flesh cannot submit to God's law.
passages.original: τὸ γὰρ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς θάνατος τὸ δὲ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος ζωὴ καὶ εἰρήνη διότι τὸ φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς ἔχθρα εἰς Θεόν τῷ γὰρ νόμῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐχ ὑποτάσσεται οὐδὲ γὰρ δύναται

passages.text: Those controlled by the flesh cannot please God.
passages.sermon:
People who live by the flesh cannot please God.
The flesh controls these people.
They do not live by the Spirit.
They do not submit to God.
They cannot do what God desires.
God is not pleased with them.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ὄντες Θεῷ ἀρέσαι οὐ δύνανται

passages.text: You, however, are controlled not by the flesh, but by the Spirit, if the Spirit of God lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.
passages.sermon:
You are not controlled by the flesh.
You are controlled by the Spirit.
This is true if the Spirit of God lives in you.
If anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐν σαρκὶ ἀλλὰ ἐν πνεύματι εἴπερ Πνεῦμα Θεοῦ οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν εἰ δέ τις Πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ οὐκ ἔχει οὗτος οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But if Christ is in you, your body is dead because of sin, yet your spirit is alive because of righteousness.
passages.sermon: Christ is in you.\r\nYour body is dead because of sin.\r\nYour spirit is alive because of righteousness.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐν ὑμῖν τὸ μὲν σῶμα νεκρὸν διὰ ἁμαρτίαν τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωὴ διὰ δικαιοσύνην

passages.text: And if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead is living in you, He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit, who lives in you.
passages.sermon:
God raised Jesus from the dead.
God’s Spirit has power over death.
If God’s Spirit lives in you, He is present in your life.
God raised Christ Jesus from the dead.
God will also give life to your mortal bodies.
He will do this through His Spirit.
His Spirit lives in you.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ τὸ Πνεῦμα τοῦ ἐγείραντος τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐκ νεκρῶν οἰκεῖ ἐν ὑμῖν ὁ ἐγείρας ἐκ νεκρῶν Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ζωοποιήσει καὶ τὰ θνητὰ σώματα ὑμῶν διὰ τοῦ ἐνοικοῦντος αὐτοῦ Πνεύματος ἐν ὑμῖν

passages.text: Therefore, brothers, we have an obligation, but it is not to the flesh, to live according to it.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to believers in Christ.
He calls them brothers.
He says, “We have an obligation.”
This obligation does not belong to the flesh.
We do not owe the flesh anything.
We are not required to live according to the flesh.
passages.original: Ἄρα οὖν ἀδελφοί ὀφειλέται ἐσμέν οὐ τῇ σαρκὶ τοῦ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆν

passages.text: For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
passages.sermon: If you live according to the flesh, you will die.\r\nIf you live by the Spirit, you put to death the deeds of the body.\r\nIf you put to death the deeds of the body by the Spirit, you will live.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ κατὰ σάρκα ζῆτε μέλλετε ἀποθνήσκειν εἰ δὲ πνεύματι τὰς πράξεις τοῦ σώματος θανατοῦτε ζήσεσθε

passages.text: For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.
passages.sermon: God leads some people by His Spirit.\r\nThese people follow the Spirit of God.\r\nThese people are sons of God.
passages.original: ὅσοι γὰρ Πνεύματι Θεοῦ ἄγονται οὗτοι υἱοί εἰσιν Θεοῦ

passages.text: For you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear, but you received the Spirit of sonship, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
passages.sermon:
You did not receive a spirit that makes you slaves.
This spirit does not bring you back to fear.
You received the Spirit that makes you sons and daughters of God.
This Spirit gives you adoption as God’s children.
By this Spirit, we call out to God.
We say, “Abba! Father!”
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα δουλείας πάλιν εἰς φόβον ἀλλὰ ἐλάβετε πνεῦμα υἱοθεσίας ἐν ᾧ κράζομεν Ἀββᾶ ὁ Πατήρ

passages.text: The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.
passages.sermon:
The Spirit is the Spirit of God.
The Spirit Himself testifies.
The Spirit testifies with our spirit.
The Spirit shows us something true.
We are God’s children.
The Spirit confirms this to us.
passages.original: αὐτὸ τὸ Πνεῦμα συμμαρτυρεῖ τῷ πνεύματι ἡμῶν ὅτι ἐσμὲν τέκνα Θεοῦ

passages.text: And if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ—if indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him.
passages.sermon:
We are God’s children.
God’s children are heirs.
We inherit from God.
We are co-heirs with Christ.
We share with Christ if we suffer with Him.
We will also share Christ’s glory if we suffer with Him.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ τέκνα καὶ κληρονόμοι κληρονόμοι μὲν Θεοῦ συνκληρονόμοι δὲ Χριστοῦ εἴπερ συμπάσχομεν ἵνα καὶ συνδοξασθῶμεν

passages.text: I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians.
Paul considers our present sufferings.
These sufferings happen now.
Paul says these sufferings are not worth comparing to future glory.
God will reveal this glory in us.
This future glory is much greater than our current pain.
passages.original: Λογίζομαι γὰρ ὅτι οὐκ ἄξια τὰ παθήματα τοῦ νῦν καιροῦ πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι εἰς ἡμᾶς

passages.text: The creation waits in eager expectation for the revelation of the sons of God.
passages.sermon:
Creation is waiting.
Creation waits with eager expectation.
Creation expects something important.
Creation waits for the sons of God to be revealed.
The sons of God will be revealed in the future.
Creation looks forward to this revelation.
passages.original: ἡ γὰρ ἀποκαραδοκία τῆς κτίσεως τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῶν υἱῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀπεκδέχεται

passages.text: For the creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and brought into the glorious freedom of the children of God.
passages.sermon:
God created everything.
God subjected creation to futility.
Creation did not choose this futility.
God did this for a purpose.
God acted in hope.
God hopes for something better for creation.
Creation now suffers under decay and corruption.
Creation is in bondage to this decay.
God plans to set creation free.
God will free creation from decay.
God will bring creation into freedom.
This freedom belongs to the children of God.
This freedom is full of glory.
passages.original: τῇ γὰρ ματαιότητι ἡ κτίσις ὑπετάγη οὐχ ἑκοῦσα ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸν ὑποτάξαντα ἐφ’ ἑλπίδι ὅτι καὶ αὐτὴ ἡ κτίσις ἐλευθερωθήσεται ἀπὸ τῆς δουλείας τῆς φθορᾶς εἰς τὴν ἐλευθερίαν τῆς δόξης τῶν τέκνων τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: We know that the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until the present time.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Roman Christians.
Paul teaches about creation.
All creation suffers.
All creation groans together.
All creation feels pain like a woman giving birth.
This pain continues until now.
passages.original: Οἴδαμεν γὰρ ὅτι πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις συστενάζει καὶ συνωδίνει ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν

passages.text: Not only that, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies.
passages.sermon:
We have the firstfruits of the Spirit.
We are believers in Christ.
We groan inwardly.
We wait eagerly for our adoption as God’s children.
We wait for the redemption of our bodies.
passages.original: οὐ μόνον δέ ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν ἀπαρχὴν τοῦ Πνεύματος ἔχοντες ἡμεῖς καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς στενάζομεν υἱοθεσίαν ἀπεκδεχόμενοι τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν τοῦ σώματος ἡμῶν

passages.text: For in this hope we were saved; but hope that is seen is no hope at all. Who hopes for what he can already see?
passages.sermon:
We are Christians who have hope in God.
God saved us through this hope.
Hope that we can already see is not real hope.
No one hopes for what he already sees.
passages.original: τῇ γὰρ ἐλπίδι ἐσώθημεν ἐλπὶς δὲ βλεπομένη οὐκ ἔστιν ἐλπίς ὃ γὰρ βλέπει τις τί ἐλπίζει

passages.text: But if we hope for what we do not yet see, we wait for it patiently.
passages.sermon:
We hope for things we do not see.
We do not see these things now.
We wait for them.
We wait with patience.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ὃ οὐ βλέπομεν ἐλπίζομεν δι’ ὑπομονῆς ἀπεκδεχόμεθα

passages.text: In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit is God’s Spirit.
The Holy Spirit helps us when we are weak.
We often do not know how to pray as we should.
The Holy Spirit prays for us.
The Holy Spirit speaks to God for us with groans too deep for words.
passages.original: Ὡσαύτως δὲ καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα συναντιλαμβάνεται τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ ἡμῶν τὸ γὰρ τί προσευξώμεθα καθὸ δεῖ οὐκ οἴδαμεν ἀλλὰ αὐτὸ τὸ Πνεῦμα ὑπερεντυγχάνει στεναγμοῖς ἀλαλήτοις

passages.text: And He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.
passages.sermon:
God searches our hearts.
God knows the mind of the Spirit.
The Spirit intercedes for the saints.
The Spirit prays according to the will of God.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ ἐραυνῶν τὰς καρδίας οἶδεν τί τὸ φρόνημα τοῦ Πνεύματος ὅτι κατὰ Θεὸν ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἁγίων

passages.text: And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.
passages.sermon:
God acts for those who love Him.
God works all things together for their good.
God calls these people according to His purpose.
We know this truth.
passages.original: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν τὸν Θεὸν πάντα συνεργεῖ ὁ θεὸς εἰς ἀγαθόν τοῖς κατὰ πρόθεσιν κλητοῖς οὖσιν

passages.text: For those God foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers.
passages.sermon:
God knows people ahead of time.
God chooses these people for a purpose.
God decides that these people will become like His Son.
God’s Son is Jesus Christ.
God wants these people to be shaped to the image of Jesus.
God does this so that Jesus will be the firstborn.
Jesus will be the first among many brothers and sisters.
passages.original: ὅτι οὓς προέγνω καὶ προώρισεν συμμόρφους τῆς εἰκόνος τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν πρωτότοκον ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς

passages.text: And those He predestined, He also called; those He called, He also justified; those He justified, He also glorified.
passages.sermon:
God predestined certain people.
God also called these people.
God called these same people.
God also justified them.
God justified these people.
God also glorified them.
passages.original: οὓς δὲ προώρισεν τούτους καὶ ἐκάλεσεν καὶ οὓς ἐκάλεσεν τούτους καὶ ἐδικαίωσεν οὓς δὲ ἐδικαίωσεν τούτους καὶ ἐδόξασεν

passages.text: What then shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
passages.sermon:
God stands for us.
No one can stand against us.
We respond to these truths with confidence.
God’s support makes us secure.
passages.original: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν πρὸς ταῦτα εἰ ὁ Θεὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τίς καθ’ ἡμῶν

passages.text: He who did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?
passages.sermon:
God did not spare His own Son.
God gave His own Son for all of us.
God gave His Son for our sake.
God will also give us all things with His Son.
God will freely give us all things along with His Son.
passages.original: ὅς γε τοῦ ἰδίου Υἱοῦ οὐκ ἐφείσατο ἀλλὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν πάντων παρέδωκεν αὐτόν πῶς οὐχὶ καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ἡμῖν χαρίσεται

passages.text: Who will bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies.
passages.sermon:
God chooses certain people.
These people are called God's elect.
No one can accuse God's elect.
God justifies His elect.
God declares them righteous.
passages.original: τίς ἐγκαλέσει κατὰ ἐκλεκτῶν Θεοῦ Θεὸς ὁ δικαιῶν

passages.text: Who is there to condemn us? For Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that was raised to life, is at the right hand of God—and He is interceding for us.
passages.sermon:
No one can condemn us.
Christ Jesus died for us.
God raised Christ Jesus to life.
Christ Jesus now sits at God’s right hand.
Christ Jesus intercedes for us.
passages.original: τίς ὁ κατακρινῶν Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀποθανών μᾶλλον δὲ ἐγερθείς ὅς καί ἐστιν ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὃς καὶ ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν

passages.text: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall trouble or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?
passages.sermon:
Christ loves us.
No one can separate us from the love of Christ.
Trouble cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
Distress cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
Persecution cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
Famine cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
Nakedness cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
Danger cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
The sword cannot separate us from Christ’s love.
passages.original: Τίς ἡμᾶς χωρίσει ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ Χριστοῦ θλῖψις ἢ στενοχωρία ἢ διωγμὸς ἢ λιμὸς ἢ γυμνότης ἢ κίνδυνος ἢ μάχαιρα

passages.text: As it is written: “For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.”
passages.sermon:
The Scripture says this.
We face death all day long for Your sake.
People count us as sheep for slaughter.
We suffer because we belong to You.
Others see us as weak and helpless.
They treat us as if we are only sheep ready to be killed.
passages.original: καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Ἕνεκεν σοῦ θανατούμεθα ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἐλογίσθημεν ὡς πρόβατα σφαγῆς

passages.text: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.
passages.sermon:
We face many troubles.
We face distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger, and the sword.
Christ loves us.
God shows His love for us in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Because Christ loves us, we overcome all these things.
We are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.
passages.original: Ἀλλ’ ἐν τούτοις πᾶσιν ὑπερνικῶμεν διὰ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντος ἡμᾶς

passages.text: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers, neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Paul is convinced of this truth.
Death cannot separate us from the love of God.
Life cannot separate us from the love of God.
Angels cannot separate us from the love of God.
Rulers or principalities cannot separate us from the love of God.
Nothing in the present can separate us from the love of God.
Nothing in the future can separate us from the love of God.
No powers can separate us from the love of God.
No height can separate us from the love of God.
No depth can separate us from the love of God.
Nothing else in all creation can separate us from the love of God.
The love of God is in Christ Jesus.
Christ Jesus is our Lord.
passages.original: πέπεισμαι γὰρ ὅτι οὔτε θάνατος οὔτε ζωὴ οὔτε ἄγγελοι οὔτε ἀρχαὶ οὔτε ἐνεστῶτα οὔτε μέλλοντα οὔτε δυνάμεις οὔτε ὕψωμα οὔτε βάθος οὔτε τις κτίσις ἑτέρα δυνήσεται ἡμᾶς χωρίσαι ἀπὸ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ Θεοῦ τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν
